author: Bc'z
notes_extra: 130 AR hybrids. Stock Remington VTR. He also tried 2.83 coal with unsorted bullets and settled on 2.80. The March 31 post repeats this charge. Start at 41 gr and work up, in that later post, is advice.

author: MikeMcCasland
notes_extra: 130 Hybrid AR. 26 in Bartlein. Lapua brass and CCI LR primers. He said H4350 accuracy was inconsistent and switched to H4831SC, about 100 fps slower, with no charge for that powder. He wrote my .260s.

author: dstoenner
notes_extra: 130 hybrid. F-Class, single loaded. COL 2.900. He started at 44 gr and backed off when it got hot. He posted the same load twice the same day. The January 10 post called 44 gr his mid-range load at around 2.900.

author: Bulletbob
notes_extra: 130 grn Bergers in the 130 AR hybrid thread. Brux 4r 1-8 twist. Groups about 1 to 1.5 MOA. The 140 Elite Hunter charges in the same post are a different bullet.

author: JBT47
notes_extra: 130 hybrids. Jump .020. His Dec 14 post gave freebore .167. He wrote 47. The thread is 6.5x47, and Berger staff identified the bullet as the 130 AR Hybrid OTM.

author: jsthntn247
notes_extra: Jump somewhere between .003 and .015. He did not name the cartridge; the thread is 6.5x47.

author: Old Navy
notes_extra: Berger 130 AR Hybrid. Aero rifle. He did not name the cartridge; the thread is 6.5 Creedmoor.

author: Bob L Swagger
notes_extra: 130 hybrids. Five shots at 100 yards off a bipod and rear bag. On Mar 12, 2015 he said 62.8 gr of H-1000 gave the best group, then backed off after the barrel picked up speed. No chronograph number.
